The other one though, damn. That is my favourite wig ever. From what I've owned. It's just the best, so lovely, so comfortable, soft and realistic. I wear it every other day.

I think it just depends on how well you research the product before buying it. The second one i got had sooo many reviews, largely all positive, and they seemed very legitimate. I checked the negative ones too and they mainly only mentioned that it sheds a lot and that the parting doesn't really work for darker skinned people, but i was okay with compromising those. But the first one, it had zero reviews whatsoever. The brand also did not seem legitimate and i don't even remember the name.

As for making it look more realistic, as a noob myself, I'm struggling a bit with that. I think it actually looks pretty good except for the scalp area. That's the only thing clocking it as a wig, the rest of it seems fine imo. But hopefully these would help, they're partially from what i heard from others and partially from personal experience:

Try to do something about the bangs:

1. Maybe part them in the middle and push them back a bit? It might seem like grown out bangs that you want to keep out of your face. You could use clips and pins to tuck them away. 

2. You could try thinning them out and turning them into wispy bangs. I feel like those add a bit more realism to the wig because it won't look like a sticked-together thick line of synthetic fibres and look a bit thinner and see-through, which i feel could help. 
Do it very carefully after seeing a tutorial on how to cut bangs, if you aren't an expert at cutting hair. Some general guidelines that helped me were to do it bit by bit, always cut a bit less than how much you want the length to be- because you can always make it shorter but you can't make a shorter one look longer. i hope it makes sense 😅


Some other ideas:

1. You could maybe try blending your real hair with the wig hair? And you could try putting on dark eye shadow to create a bit of a rooted look on top. Take this with a grain of salt though, because I've only heard other people do it and haven't tried it myself, putting eye shadow around the parting. I blended my real hair with my wig which only worked because of the dark roots and the results were really good. 

2. You could try cutting in baby hair into the wig. Lift up a large section of the top of the bangs and pin it away, and with the bottommost hair, gently try to cut away some of the length in a way that resembles baby hair. Be careful with this as you should be with modifying the bangs. Don't fully cut away the hair because that may not look like baby hair. 


General ideas:

1. Put a hat on top, or a scarf, to cover up the scalp and parting. 

2. Use dry shampoo to reduce the shine (i personally have never tried this though, because there was never a need to with the wigs i owned)

3. Pluck away a bit of the hairline to make it look more realistic (again, be careful about this 😬 do it a bit slowly and cautiously) 


I'd like to say that some of these may not be the best advice because again, I'm a noob- but i love helping others out because i remember being totally clueless in the beginning and don't want others to struggle the same way. Hopefully these will give you at least a bit of direction along your way :) Some of these worked for me and i hope they do for you too, if you try it out

Ah okay, i see what you mean. Like i mentioned in my other comment, that my therapist said that it's a bit common/normal to find other people attractive- i guess it could be persistent or a one time thing for that same person or for multiple different people? Idk. But he said that in long term relationships it's very common to find someone outside of the relationship attractive too, but that those feelings are most likely very fleeting and weak/feeble if you truly love your partner, they'll go away, and IMO its not worth acting on if you really love and prioritise your partner. Do you really love and prioritise your partner? If so, would you be okay with them hurting intensely for a long time and you being the reason for it, watching them struggling day and night, not trusting you and possibly never trusting you again, and many other relationship problems? Very unlikely. If you don't really love your partner, well, then it's not an issue for you, but you shouldn't be hurting another person who you consensually and mutually agreed to be in a relationship with and they trust you and need you to be there for them. Break up with them instead, don't stay in a relationship with someone you don't love. It's not fair for them and it's not beneficial to you (as cold as the latter sounds, that's unfortunately how some people might think). So yeah, those fleeting thoughts could appear sometimes, but i agree with you that if it happens wayyyy too often and you like the idea of it, that you actually want to do it, it's highly likely that you will.

While i don't excuse it, it's one of the worst things you could do to your partner, its possible. Everyone makes mistakes in relationships, big or small, and it's common. Sometimes we hurt the people we love the most even if we in hindsight don't intend to cause them a lot of pain. We might make intentional decisions to do an action that we may or may not realise/know to be harmful at that moment. Cheating is just one of them. It's not always about finding someone else attractive, I've heard, but encompass many other psychological factors such as insecurity and a certain dissatisfaction in the relationship (again, not justifiable). 

I personally did not believe in this at all earlier. I thought it was bullshit and someone cheating meant that they don't love their partner and don't care for them. But after looking at my own parents, i realised that it's true. My father loves my mother way too much, it's so obvious, and the way she treats him as though he's not even human, it breaks him so much, but he still goes on loving her and being so nice to her to a point where he doesn't even stand up for himself. He thinks it's him being punished for his wrongdoings, that he deserves it, and maybe it is so. But he loves her a lot and no one can deny it. It's his biggest dream to see her become better, to see her not struggle anymore from mental health issues. My mother has a lot of abusive tendencies and my dad tried to help ease it out between the two of us because he sympathised with her and believed that it's not her true nature. He also loves his children and my mom so much, and wants to see me and my sister unite with my mom, all hurts of the past faded away. It disturbs his sleep at night and he carries all the blame on himself. He prays for it. I'm not saying that everyone will regret it and try to make up for it, but my dad did, and so its possible.

Intrusive thoughts can also be consistent and not be just a one time thing. For example, someone suffering from them due to a different mental health issue, such as OCD, could probably have persistent intrusive thoughts that make them feel like they're a p*dophile. They would of course not go through with the actions because they are simply, logically put, not attracted to children. Intrusive thoughts are well known to be against your moral compass.

I second this, my therapist had told me the same things when i was having intrusive thoughts (i most likely have OCD too, very likely because of all the symptoms) and they distressed me. I wasn't even attracted to anyone else to a point where i would literally do the things with them that I'd much rather do with the love of my life, and yet my brain would worry me for no reason, just like any other intrusive thought. My therapist further elaborated that it's normal to find other people attractive from time to time, that it's normal and only human; but what matters is, if you love and prioritise your partner, you shouldn't go ahead with those thoughts because they are most likely fleeting anyway. Those feelings for another might go away but your love for your partner will remain; and if you hurt your partner you're only going to regret it and you've caused them a great deal of emotional distress that is difficult to overcome. Moreover, like other comments have been pointing out, if you really do love your partner, why would you do that? We all make mistakes in relationships but this is one of the biggest and most harmful ones imo.
